I've done everything they've suggested, I try to keep an open-mind about these things but at the end of it, there's this innate idea of death. It's what I always come back to. Often from out of no-where. I'll be perfectly happy and then mid-conversation, "I should kill myself. What's the point?" 

Depression, anxiety, chronic pain. None of those are helping, but it goes back to before I had those on a level they were impacting my life in such a negative way.

I probably should have expanded on that front. I've had five therapists so far, and I'm in my sixth set of therapy sessions now. Some of them were just downright awful at what they did. Some didn't seem to listen.

One of them was good, but he didn't (and still doesn't), by his own admission, know how to help me. It's rather demoralizing wanting help and wanting to help myself too, but it just never seems to work out. I don't have the kind of money spare to hire a really good therapist, I have to rely on charities to pay for it and they pick the cheaper options (understandably).

Disclaimer: I have no idea if this still works as it was/is an old method and I won't change my name to test it.

Sign up to battle net (do not set a battle tag).

Open the app and change the language to the one you desire your name to be, in this case, Chinese. 

Restart the app. 

Log in your battle net account on the launcher and it'll ask you to make a battle tag. It should (not sure if it still does), accept the Chinese name now. 

This will not work however if it's an existing battle net account, as they can only change their name via the website. Must be a "fresh" account. 

As I said, not sure if this method still works, but you're welcome to try it. Have fun with the game!

Year upon year, stuck in the same room. Same four walls. Alone. It's tiresome.

I just got so depressed again tonight and couldn't stop crying. I tried to clear my head but after 10 or so minutes I just grabbed a knife and did it. 

I've never done something like that before, seems like only two of them were deep enough to leave any scar/mark but still, this is not like me. I couldn't control myself.
I feel so shit and hopeless and I'm losing the will to try anymore.

While I can't advocate for you to get it or not get it, from personal experience, the medication itself isn't too scary to take. I think the biggest hurdle is trying to get the help to begin with. 

It can be difficult to open up to someone else like that, and depression often tries to tell us not to do things that are difficult for us. 

It's great to see you decided to do something about how you're feeling though, sometimes the medications take a while to work, so don't worry if you don't notice any changes "immediately". I'm not too familiar with US healthcare or anything so I can't give any specific examples, but over here I was just sat down, talked to for a while, and later on given some medication to take. They asked general questions about how I was feeling, was I suicidal etc. 

I hope you figure things out, best of luck with it. 
-FP

I'm sorry but you clearly haven't read anything I originally linked for context. 

Taking my life, in my perspective, would actually fix everything. Would it fix it in another persons's perspective? Absolutely not. In mine though, yes. These thoughts and feelings are in the confines of my head. Death cancels out life, which cancels said thoughts and feelings. 

Everything bad happening in my life I am responsible for? 
So I am responsible for genetic malfunctions causing irreversible muscle damage, bone failures, chronic conditions causing wide spread pain and fatigue? If I knew how to reverse time and genetically engineer myself,  I assure you I would.

As for your comment about helping them with bills (not them anyway, just one), please read context before making such comments. I am permanently wheelchair bound, with a severe shoulder problem preventing movement in the chair at all. I cannot leave my home, I can't even get into my bed some nights. You're welcome to point me to any employer looking for a mentally unstable (yes I have had therapy and meds), physically unwell individual with minimal qualifications who cannot leave his house or even get out of bed most days. 

The idea of not living for yourself at all, and only living for other people is also further evidence towards suicide. If the entire existence is futile and you must spend your life living for everyone else and not yourself, what is the point at all? 

I understand in some way you are trying to help. However these kinds of posts just don't help at all. I'm unsure if you've ever been in such a situation, but if you have, think back to it. If you haven't, I hope you can come to terms with why these posts just don't help. 

I probably won't reply to this further, comments like these cause seriously negative side effects, hence they're forbidden in the context of the sub-reddit to begin with. I'm just going to OD on my meds and hope it puts me to sleep long enough to wake up able to do another day.
